Class 4 · Chapter 7 of 9

Bills, budgets and rupees with paise

Keep rupees and paise lined up while comparing real shopping choices.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Timetables, dates and clock errors. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can total a bill and find change.
  • I can compare equal amounts in packs.
  • I can choose within a budget.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Add up the bill

Add the prices one at a time.

Rs 50 + Rs 20 + Rs 5 = Rs 75.

Keep rupees under rupees when you write them in a column.

Screen 2 of 4

Find the change

Pay Rs 200 for a Rs 130 bill.

Count on: 130 to 150 is 20. 150 to 200 is 50.

The change is Rs 70.

Screen 3 of 4

Compare packs

Pack A has 6 pens for Rs 30. That is Rs 5 each.

Pack B has 4 pens for Rs 24. That is Rs 6 each.

Pack A is the better buy.

Screen 4 of 4

Rupees and paise

100 paise make Rs 1.

Rs 2.50 means 2 rupees and 50 paise.

Line up the point before you add.

Words to know
bill
The list of what you bought and the total you owe.
change
The money you get back when you pay more than the bill.
budget
The most money you plan to spend.
paise
100 paise make 1 rupee.

For parents

What your child learns

Money problems often have several steps. Multiply to find the cost of many items, add the bills, then subtract from what was paid. Savings are what you earn minus what you spend.

A common slip

Children often stop after the first step. Write each step on its own line and tick when done. Reread the question to check what is asked.

5-minute home activity: Make a receipt

  1. Write a receipt with 5 items at Rs 56 each.
  2. Add one more item.
  3. Subtract the total from Rs 1000 to find the change.
  4. Work out weekly savings for 3 weeks.
